source.title: Multilingual Blending: LLM Safety Alignment Evaluation with Language Mixture
source.authors: Jia-Yang Song; Yu-Heng Huang; Zhehua Zhou; Lei Ma

record.tranche_reason: The study tests safety-alignment bypass through multilingual query and response formatting, a different intervention from the versions' fine-tuning, first-token KL, opening-token, parameter-localization, or deepening tests.
record.gate_note: The study reports multilingual attack bypass rates and first-token entropy measurements. The bypass-rate results concern safety behavior but do not test any listed version's specified mechanism; they are recorded as findings outside the versions. The entropy results are not KL divergence between aligned and base models. Fine-tuning, compliant-opening prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, safety-localized weights, and deepening training are not tested.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a multilingual input/output-format jailbreak (Multilingual Blending) on GPT-3.5, GPT-4o and five open models. It does no fine-tuning (V1, V2) and compares no aligned and base per-token distributions (V3). It uses no compliant-opening prefill, adversarial suffix or decoding change (V4), and tests neither parameter localization (V5), the causes of shallowness (V6) nor deepening training (V7). Qi et al. 2023, an original source, is cited only as an example of supervised fine-tuning for alignment. A prompt-transformation jailbreak is a different construct from V4's opening-token bypass, so the record's 'tests'/T2 is wrong. The bypass-rate results belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that mixed-language queries with mixed-language responses undermine safety alignment across GPT and open models. They find that resource level, morphology and language family modulate effectiveness, and call for multilingual-aware safety evaluation and alignment.
record.recipe_differences: This is a multilingual prompt-and-response-format attack evaluation, not fine-tuning or a test of first-token distribution concentration.
record.method_sensitivity: Bypass rates vary with query/response format, number and resource level of languages, morphology, language family, and model. English-query/mixed-response cases had 0.00% bypass for GPT-4o, while mixed-query/mixed-response cases were higher; the study also reports lower rates when language mixtures are too few or too many than around four languages.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixed-language queries with mixed-language response instructions raise bypass rates (Perspective API judged) above English baselines. Examples: GPT-3.5 from 1.67% to 67.23% and GPT-4o from 0% to 40.34%. Open models rise from 1.67–5.83% to 11.76–42.37%. Rates vary with resource level, morphology and language family.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multilingual blended query-and-response formatting bypasses safety alignment in chat models, with effectiveness depending on the language mixture.

fits_no_version.finding: First-token Shannon entropy (Table 6) is higher for bypassed than safe responses, and higher in mixed-language than single-language settings (about 120% for safe cases and 52% for bypassed). This is a confidence measure on the aligned model only, not an aligned-versus-base KL.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: First-token uncertainty rises when safety alignment is bypassed and under mixed-language inputs.

record.problems: The study uses a selected set of 120 malicious questions and a Perspective API evaluator with a stated threshold. It reports no uncertainty intervals for bypass rates. It notes limited language and combination coverage and uses token-level random translation. The authors say Llama3-8B cannot follow the mixed-language response format, complicating interpretation. Table 8 has inconsistent format labels for the mixed-query/English-response rows, clarified only partly by the appendix description and system prompts.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within the 60-row limit, omitted the remaining separately reported conditions in Tables 1–5 and 7–8, including most language-by-language baselines, number-of-languages and resource-level sweeps, morphology and family combinations, and additional combinations for the open models. Table 6's first-token entropy values were also omitted because they do not measure harmful-compliance behavior or aligned-versus-base per-token KL. The selected rows retain all three formats and combinations in the ablation (Table 8), one single and one mixed condition per open model (Table 7), the two headline mixed-morphology maxima (Table 4), and English baselines (Table 1).

untested.parts: No per-token KL between aligned and base models. Table 6 reports first-token entropy of the aligned model only.
No prefilling of a compliant start, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes. The attack transforms the query language and requests a mixed-language response format.
No analysis of whether data or the training objective causes shallowness.
No deepening training or robustness test of it.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation (tests) and tranche (T2) are overturned. No version is tested, so no verdicts are given. Row states remain cannot_determine with versions ['none']. The evaluator is Perspective API toxicity attributes at a 0.3 threshold on back-translated outputs, a weak proxy for harmful compliance. Llama3-8B could not follow the mixed-language output instruction, which the authors note complicates interpretation of its rates.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and refusal after fine-tuning.
Benign-data fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
Compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes. The tested multilingual input/output-format attack is a different intervention.
Localization of safety behavior in weights or ranks.
Whether data or training objectives cause first-token shallowness.
Training that deepens safety across response tokens and its robustness.

relation.reason: Qi et al. 2023 is cited as background on supervised safety alignment; the study neither tests its fine-tuning finding nor uses shallow alignment as a tool.

tranche.reason: The study tests multilingual query and response formats, without testing or using any listed claim version. Its first-token entropy analysis does not compare aligned and base distributions or measure concentration across response positions.

source_check.notes: Bypass rates use Perspective API on English back-translations, with any of ten attributes exceeding 0.3 counted unsafe. Table 8's second scheme has an English-Query label typo; its caption and system prompt establish English responses.
